chunks: Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) say: 'By Allah, a man from us, the Ahl al-Bayt, will rule after his death for three hundred and nine years.' I asked: 'When will this be?' He replied: 'After the Qaim (peace be upon him).' I asked: 'For how many years will the Qaim rule in his world?' He replied: 'Nineteen years. Then the Muntasir will emerge and seek revenge for the blood of Husayn (peace be upon him) and the blood of his companions, killing and capturing until the Saffah emerges.'

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيْتِ: Ahl al-Bayt (the Family of the Prophet)
key_terms.الصَّفَّاحُ: The Saffah (a title for a future ruler, often associated with the Abbasids or a specific Imam)
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Qaim (the Rising One, referring to Imam al-Mahdi)
key_terms.الْمُنْتَصِرُ: The Avenger (referring to Imam Husayn or a specific figure seeking vengeance)

ai.seo_question: How long will the rule of the Ahl al-Bayt last after the Qaim according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* outlines the eschatological timeline of the Ahl al-Bayt's rule, specifying a 309-year reign following the 19-year era of the Qaim. It highlights the sequential emergence of the Muntasir, who avenges the blood of Imam Husayn, and the Saffah, establishing a distinct period of justice and retribution within Shia eschatology. The narration underscores the continuity of Imamate authority and the fulfillment of divine promise regarding the inheritance of the earth by the righteous servants.
